turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - alloy_pair_max_train.csv: 300 samples described by composition in wt% — C, Mn, Si, Cr, Ni, Mo, V, Nb, Co, Al, Ti, Cu
      (Fe is the balance: Fe = 100 − Σ of the others) — plus processing parameters
      (solutionizing_temp, aging_temp, aging_time, cooling_rate) and categorical
      settings heat_treatment (annealed | quenched | quench_temper | solution_aged)
      and route (cast | wrought | AM), with the measured 0.2 % proof yield strength in MPa (the `target` column).
  - alloy_pair_max_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE recipes whose yield strength was NOT measured, with the same columns plus `candidate_id` and no `target`.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST yield strength (MPa), then select the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Approach

**Step 1 — Identify processing effects.** Sorting the training data by target, the top ~15 samples (610–713 MPa) are overwhelmingly **solution_aged + wrought** (e.g., 712.9, 697.9, 693.9, 676.7, 674.2, 668.2, 652.3, 648.7, 648.6, 647.2 MPa). Quench_temper tops out ~611 MPa, quenched ~557, and annealed is systematically weakest (many <250 MPa). Route ordering is roughly wrought > AM > cast.

**Step 2 — Processing-parameter sweet spot.** The top performers have **aging_temp ≈ 600–735 °C**, with aging_time and solutionizing temp mattering little; cooling rate is tolerant over a wide range.

**Step 3 — Composition trends among the best.** Winners have moderate C (0.1–0.6), Ni ~5–17, Cr ~1–15, Mo 0–4, Co 0–9, and **avoid stacked extremes** (C=1.2, Mo=6, Al=2 + Ti=1.5 combinations correlate with low strength, especially outside solution_aged/wrought).

**Step 4 — Screen the pool.** Only 9 candidates are solution_aged + wrought: c008, c015, c021, c038, c048, c052, c053, c069, c072. Matching each against nearest training analogs:

- **c008** (Ni 13, Mo 3.9, Co 8.4, Al 0.12, aging 683 °C): nearly clones the 697.9 / 712.9 MPa winners → predicted ~660–700 MPa.
- **c072** (Ni 9.3, Mo 2.7, Co 7.4, Al 0.05, aging 750 °C): matches the 648.6 / 697.9 MPa recipes → ~640–690 MPa.
- **c053** (Cr 16.3, Ni 12.4, aging 730 °C): close analog of the 693.9 MPa sample (Cr 14.4, Ni 15.7, aging 709 °C); high Al is tolerated in this class (615–629 MPa samples had Al 1.5–2.0) → ~620–670 MPa.
- **c038** (Cr 4.9, Ni 11.4, aging 608 °C, low Al): analogs at 619.4 and 570 MPa → ~600–640 MPa.
- **c021** (Cr 13.4, Ni 7.7, aging 592 °C, cooling 75): analogs 611.3 and 591.4 MPa → ~590–630 MPa.

Runners-up: c015 (~590, hurt by cooling rate 0.1 and Co=0), c052 (Ni=0), c069/c048 (aging temp too low, ~500–550). The best quench_temper candidates (c028, c050, c062) project only ~530–550 MPa, below all five picks.

**Final: c008, c072, c053, c038, c021**
